observations: Photo 0: A gray metal automatic transmission case with wiring harness, black coolant/vent hose, and braided conduit; sits on a workbench with a yellow painted wood backdrop.

Photo 1: Close-up of the transmission bellhousing showing a torque converter with visible surface rust/staining and a partial stamped marking that looks like '22K' on the converter face; no manufacturer name or part number plate visible.

Photo 2: Wider shot showing the same transmission from another angle, with a separate V-engine block in the background (not part of this listing), sitting on the same workbench with sandals/shoes nearby.
No VIN tag, casting number, or 'Dodge' / 'Caliber' text is visible or legible in any photo.
Watermarks read 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'GEARUP INC' — these are platform/seller marks, not part identification.

claims.evidence: No casting number, tag, or model stamp reading 'Dodge' or 'Caliber' is visible in photo 0, 1, or 2.
No documentation, import sticker, or origin marking shown in any photo.
No warranty card, receipt, or shop stamp is shown in any photo.

risks.risk: Transmission model/fitment cannot be confirmed, so it may not match the claimed Dodge Caliber application.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped casting number or ID tag on the transmission case (usually on the bellhousing flange or top of the case).
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic used automatic transmission, not as Dodge Caliber-specific part

risks.risk: Internal condition (clutch packs, gears, valve body) cannot be assessed from exterior photos; torque converter shows surface rust/wear.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being turned over by hand or bench-tested, or a shop inspection report.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / condition unknown, salvage-grade

risks.risk: The '22K' stamp on the torque converter is unexplained — could be a part/batch code, not mileage; mileage claims cannot be trusted.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any odometer/mileage document or donor-vehicle paperwork tied to this specific unit.

risks.risk: Wiring harness connectors and solenoids appear intact but electrical/hydraulic function is unverified.
risks.proof: Clip of solenoids being bench-tested or continuity-checked.

risks.risk: No fluid pan or drain plug images, so fluid condition/leak history is unknown.
risks.proof: Photo of the fluid pan, drain plug, and dipstick/fill area.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible fluid contamination or leaks

proof_requests: Close-up, well-lit photo of the stamped casting/part number or ID tag on the transmission case confirming make and model.
Any paperwork, receipt, or warranty document referenced as 'warranty attached'.
Photo or video of the transmission being rotated/tested to show the gears turn freely and torque converter spins without binding.
Photo of the fluid pan and drain plug area for leak/contamination assessment.
response.reason: The seller names a specific vehicle model (Dodge Caliber) that would set the price category, but no tag, casting number, or marking in any photo confirms this identity, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored to the right part class without that proof.
